title: Spark / PySpark
interviewAnswer: Spark distributes transformations over partitions of large datasets. DataFrames and Spark SQL provide optimized execution while lazy evaluation lets Spark build an execution plan before running actions.
why: Spark/PySpark is common in data engineering and ML pipelines because it provides distributed DataFrame/SQL processing across large datasets.
intuition: Spark builds a logical plan from transformations and executes it lazily across partitions. It moves computation to distributed workers rather than loading all data into one Python process.
deepDive: Transformations are lazy; actions trigger execution. Narrow transformations can operate partition-locally, while wide transformations require shuffles and are expensive. Spark SQL/DataFrames benefit from Catalyst optimization and Tungsten execution. Partition count, skew, joins, caching and serialization dominate performance. PySpark UDFs can cross Python/JVM boundaries and are often slower than built-in expressions.
workedExample: A large join on a skewed customer_id can send huge data to one reducer. Salting, better partitioning or broadcast joins for small dimension tables can reduce the bottleneck.
commonMistakes: Calling collect() on a dataset too large for the driver.
Using Python UDFs where built-in Spark SQL functions exist.
followUps: How do you handle data skew?
production: Monitor stage/task time, shuffle size, executor memory/GC and skew. Partition output files sensibly to avoid both giant files and millions of tiny files.
